q: 我们三个人___喜欢踢足球。
zh: 我们三个人都喜欢踢足球。
py: wǒ men sān gè rén dōu xǐ huan tī zú qiú
en: All three of us like playing football.
why: 都 totals 我们三个人 and sits right before 喜欢. 也 would add 'too', which the English does not say.

q: 这两件衣服___很便宜。
zh: 这两件衣服都很便宜。
py: zhè liǎng jiàn yī fu dōu hěn pián yi
en: Both of these garments are very cheap.
why: Two items are totalled, so 都 goes before 很便宜 (Chinese has no separate 'both'). 也 would mean 'also cheap' and needs an earlier cheap thing.

q: 这几天商店里的东西___在打折。
zh: 这几天商店里的东西都在打折。
py: zhè jǐ tiān shāng diàn lǐ de dōng xi dōu zài dǎ zhé
en: All the things in the shop have been on sale these past few days.
why: 都 totals the plural 东西 and stands before 在打折. 也 'also' and 又 'again' add meanings the English does not have.

q: 孩子们___想跟爸爸一起去爬山。
zh: 孩子们都想跟爸爸一起去爬山。
py: hái zi men dōu xiǎng gēn bà ba yī qǐ qù pá shān
en: The children all want to go hiking with Dad.
why: 都 follows the plural subject 孩子们 and comes before the modal 想. The cue says 'all', not 'too', so 也 is wrong.

q: 那些衣服我___买下来了。
zh: 那些衣服我都买下来了。
py: nà xiē yī fu wǒ dōu mǎi xià lái le
en: I bought all of those clothes.
why: The object 那些衣服 is fronted so 都 can total it. 也 would mean 'I bought those too'; 才 means 'only then' and does not fit.

q: 我喜欢游泳，我哥哥___喜欢。
zh: 我喜欢游泳，我哥哥也喜欢。
py: wǒ xǐ huan yóu yǒng wǒ gē ge yě xǐ huan
en: I like swimming; my older brother likes it too.
why: The English says 'too', so 也 goes after 我哥哥 before 喜欢. 都 needs a plural subject; one brother gives it nothing to total.

q: 你买这个，我___买这个。
zh: 你买这个，我也买这个。
py: nǐ mǎi zhè ge wǒ yě mǎi zhè ge
en: You're buying this one; I'm buying this one too.
why: 也 means 'too' and stands after the subject 我. 又 means 'again', which is not what is said.

q: 这个球拍很便宜，那个___很便宜。
zh: 这个球拍很便宜，那个也很便宜。
py: zhè ge qiú pāi hěn pián yi nà ge yě hěn pián yi
en: This racket is cheap; that one is cheap too.
why: 'That one is cheap too' needs 也 before 很. 都 would total several things but 那个 is one racket.

q: 我周末在公园跑步，小王周末___在公园跑步。
zh: 我周末在公园跑步，小王周末也在公园跑步。
py: wǒ zhōu mò zài gōng yuán pǎo bù xiǎo wáng zhōu mò yě zài gōng yuán pǎo bù
en: I run in the park at weekends; Xiao Wang runs in the park at weekends too.
why: 也 follows the subject (and the time word) and comes before the 在公园 phrase. 又 would mean the same person does it again.

q: 我对打羽毛球很感兴趣，他___对羽毛球很感兴趣，所以我们常常一起打。
zh: 我对打羽毛球很感兴趣，他也对羽毛球很感兴趣，所以我们常常一起打。
py: wǒ duì dǎ yǔ máo qiú hěn gǎn xìng qù tā yě duì yǔ máo qiú hěn gǎn xìng qù suǒ yǐ wǒ men cháng cháng yī qǐ dǎ
en: I am keen on badminton and he is keen on it too, so we often play together.
why: 'He too' is 他也, and 也 sits before the 对 phrase. 又 adds a repetition meaning, not 'too'.

q: 这家店的鞋很好看，价格___很合适。
zh: 这家店的鞋很好看，价格也很合适。
py: zhè jiā diàn de xié hěn hǎo kàn jià gé yě hěn hé shì
en: The shoes in this shop look good, and the price is also very reasonable.
why: 'Also' for a second quality is 也, placed after 价格 before 很. 都 would need several things to total.

q: 我们___买了新鞋。
zh: 我们也都买了新鞋。
py: wǒ men yě dōu mǎi le xīn xié
en: We all bought new shoes too.
why: When both are needed, 也 comes first: 也都. 都也 is impossible.

q: 你的朋友都喜欢踢足球，我的朋友___喜欢。
zh: 你的朋友都喜欢踢足球，我的朋友也都喜欢。
py: nǐ de péng you dōu xǐ huan tī zú qiú wǒ de péng you yě dōu xǐ huan
en: All your friends like football; all my friends like it too.
why: 'All ... too' needs both adverbs, and the fixed order is 也都. 都也 is never said.

q: 这家店的肉很便宜，这些菜___很便宜。
zh: 这家店的肉很便宜，这些菜也都很便宜。
py: zhè jiā diàn de ròu hěn pián yi zhè xiē cài yě dōu hěn pián yi
en: The meat in this shop is cheap, and these vegetables are all cheap too.
why: Another cheap thing ('too') plus a plural total ('all') gives 也都 before 很. The reverse order 都也 does not exist.

q: 他们俩都是篮球迷，我和我弟弟___是，所以周末我们四个常常一起看比赛。
zh: 他们俩都是篮球迷，我和我弟弟也都是，所以周末我们四个常常一起看比赛。
py: tā men liǎ dōu shì lán qiú mí wǒ hé wǒ dì di yě dōu shì suǒ yǐ zhōu mò wǒ men sì gè cháng cháng yī qǐ kàn bǐ sài
en: Both of them are basketball fans, and my younger brother and I are both fans too, so the four of us often watch games together on weekends.
why: Both 也 ('too') and 都 ('both') are needed, and 也 must precede 都. 都也 is not Chinese.

q: 大人爱吃苹果，孩子们___爱吃。
zh: 大人爱吃苹果，孩子们也都爱吃。
py: dà ren ài chī píng guǒ hái zi men yě dōu ài chī
en: Adults love eating apples, and the children all love them too.
why: 'Too' (也) and 'all' (都) together are always in the order 也都.

q: 我___喜欢这家店，东西太贵了。
zh: 我也不喜欢这家店，东西太贵了。
py: wǒ yě bù xǐ huan zhè jiā diàn dōng xi tài guì le
en: I don't like this shop either; things are too expensive.
why: 'Not ... either' is 也不: 也 comes before 不. 不也 is the wrong order in a plain statement.

q: 下雨了，我们___没去商店。
zh: 下雨了，我们都没去商店。
py: xià yǔ le wǒ men dōu méi qù shāng diàn
en: It was raining, so none of us went to the shop.
why: 都没 means none of us. 也没 would mean 'we didn't go either', which needs an earlier person who also stayed home.

q: 昨天下雨，所以我们___去踢球。
zh: 昨天下雨，所以我们都没去踢球。
py: zuó tiān xià yǔ suǒ yǐ wǒ men dōu méi qù tī qiú
en: It rained yesterday, so none of us went to play football.
why: 都 comes before 没: 都没去 means none went. 没都 is not a possible order.

q: 这些球员___是中国人，有两个是美国人。
zh: 这些球员不都是中国人，有两个是美国人。
py: zhè xiē qiú yuán bù dōu shì zhōng guó rén yǒu liǎng gè shì měi guó rén
en: Not all of these players are Chinese; two are American.
why: 不都 means not all. 都不是 would say none are Chinese, which contradicts the Chinese players implied by 'two are American' as a partial case.

q: 这几家店我___去过，所以哪家好我一点儿也不知道。
zh: 这几家店我都没去过，所以哪家好我一点儿也不知道。
py: zhè jǐ jiā diàn wǒ dōu méi qù guo suǒ yǐ nǎ jiā hǎo wǒ yī diǎn r yě bù zhī dào
en: I haven't been to any of these shops, so I have no idea which is good.
why: 'None' is 都没. 不都 would mean not all, implying I know some of them, which clashes with having no idea.

q: 来看比赛的人___是学生，也有老师。
zh: 来看比赛的人不都是学生，也有老师。
py: lái kàn bǐ sài de rén bù dōu shì xué sheng yě yǒu lǎo shī
en: Not all the people who came to watch the match are students; there are teachers too.
why: 'Not all' is 不都. 都不是 would mean no one is a student, which clashes with 也有老师 ('there are also teachers').

q: 这个牌子的运动鞋太贵了，我们___想买，所以只好去别的店看看。
zh: 这个牌子的运动鞋太贵了，我们都不想买，所以只好去别的店看看。
py: zhè ge pái zi de yùn dòng xié tài guì le wǒ men dōu bù xiǎng mǎi suǒ yǐ zhǐ hǎo qù bié de diàn kàn kan
en: These sneakers are too expensive; none of us wants to buy them, so we have to look in other shops.
why: 'None of us' is 都不. 不都 would only say some do not want them, and then there would be no need to leave the shop.

q: 票价___是一样的，学生票比成人票便宜。
zh: 票价不都是一样的，学生票比成人票便宜。
py: piào jià bù dōu shì yī yàng de xué sheng piào bǐ chéng rén piào pián yi
en: Ticket prices are not all the same; student tickets are cheaper than adult ones.
why: 'Not all the same' is 不都. 都不 would say that none of them is the same, which is a different claim.

q: 我每天晚上___去公园跑步。
zh: 我每天晚上都去公园跑步。
py: wǒ měi tiān wǎn shang dōu qù gōng yuán pǎo bù
en: I go running in the park every evening.
why: A 每 phrase is followed by 都 before the verb. 也 would add 'too'; 才 means 'only then'.

q: 每个人___喜欢这家商店。
zh: 每个人都喜欢这家商店。
py: měi gè rén dōu xǐ huan zhè jiā shāng diàn
en: Everyone likes this shop.
why: 每个人 needs 都 before the verb. 也 would mean 'also' and has no earlier person to refer back to.

q: 他每次买东西___要问价格。
zh: 他每次买东西都要问价格。
py: tā měi cì mǎi dōng xi dōu yào wèn jià gé
en: Every time he shops he asks the price.
why: 每次 is followed by 都 before the predicate. 才 and 又 do not mean 'every time'.

q: 我们班每个同学___参加了学校的足球比赛。
zh: 我们班每个同学都参加了学校的足球比赛。
py: wǒ men bān měi gè tóng xué dōu cān jiā le xué xiào de zú qiú bǐ sài
en: Every student in our class took part in the school football match.
why: 每个同学 calls for 都 before 参加. 也 would only mean 'also took part'.

q: 每次比赛前我___很紧张。
zh: 每次比赛前我都很紧张。
py: měi cì bǐ sài qián wǒ dōu hěn jǐn zhāng
en: I am nervous before every match.
why: 'Every time' is marked by 都 after the subject, before 很紧张. 又 'again' and 也 'also' do not express 'every'.

q: 这家商店的东西每件___打八折，所以周末来买东西的人特别多。
zh: 这家商店的东西每件都打八折，所以周末来买东西的人特别多。
py: zhè jiā shāng diàn de dōng xi měi jiàn dōu dǎ bā zhé suǒ yǐ zhōu mò lái mǎi dōng xi de rén tè bié duō
en: Every item in this shop is 20 percent off, so a great many people come shopping at the weekend.
why: 每件 is closed off by 都 before 打八折. 也 would mean 'also 20 percent off'.

q: 我什么___想买。
zh: 我什么都想买。
py: wǒ shén me dōu xiǎng mǎi
en: I want to buy everything.
why: 什么 + 都 means 'everything'. The question word comes before 都, even though it is the object.

q: 谁___知道他是有名的足球运动员。
zh: 谁都知道他是有名的足球运动员。
py: shéi dōu zhī dào tā shì yǒu míng de zú qiú yùn dòng yuán
en: Everyone knows he is a famous football player.
why: 谁 + 都 means 'everyone'. In a positive sentence 都 is the word to use; 也 would mean 'also'.

q: 今天太累了，我___想去。
zh: 今天太累了，我哪儿都不想去。
py: jīn tiān tài lèi le wǒ nǎ r dōu bù xiǎng qù
en: I'm too tired today; I don't want to go anywhere.
why: The pattern is question word, then 都, then 不. 不哪儿都 breaks the order; 哪儿都想去 says the opposite.

q: 钱包忘在家里了，我什么___没买。
zh: 钱包忘在家里了，我什么都没买。
py: qián bāo wàng zài jiā lǐ le wǒ shén me dōu méi mǎi
en: I left my wallet at home, so I bought nothing.
why: 什么 + 都 + 没 means 'nothing at all'. 还 would turn it into 'haven't bought anything yet'.

q: 你想买哪个颜色？我哪个___可以，你选吧。
zh: 你想买哪个颜色？我哪个都可以，你选吧。
py: nǐ xiǎng mǎi nǎ ge yán sè wǒ nǎ ge dōu kě yǐ nǐ xuǎn ba
en: Which colour do you want to buy? Any one is fine with me; you choose.
why: 哪个 + 都 + 可以 means 'any is fine'. The question word precedes 都 and 才/又 cannot take this meaning.

q: 他对运动很感兴趣，什么运动他___愿意试一试。
zh: 他对运动很感兴趣，什么运动他都愿意试一试。
py: tā duì yùn dòng hěn gǎn xìng qù shén me yùn dòng tā dōu yuàn yì shì yī shì
en: He loves sport and is willing to try any sport.
why: 什么运动 is fronted and totalled by 都 ('any sport'). 也 is only for negatives or 'also' and does not give 'any' here.

q: 我今天一点儿___不累。
zh: 我今天一点儿也不累。
py: wǒ jīn tiān yī diǎn r yě bù lèi
en: I'm not tired at all today.
why: 一点儿 is followed by 也 (or 都), then 不. 还 and 又 cannot sit in this slot.

q: 他一分钱___没带，所以不能买东西。
zh: 他一分钱也没带，所以不能买东西。
py: tā yī fēn qián yě méi dài suǒ yǐ bù néng mǎi dōng xi
en: He didn't bring a single cent, so he can't buy anything.
why: 'Not a single cent' is 一分钱 + 也 + 没. 才 and 就 do not give 'not even one'.

q: 那家店的衣服，我一件___没买。
zh: 那家店的衣服，我一件都没买。
py: nà jiā diàn de yī fu wǒ yī jiàn dōu méi mǎi
en: I didn't buy a single item from that shop.
why: 一 + measure + 都/也 + 没 means 'not even one'. 就 and 才 do not fit before 没 in this meaning.

q: 这个价格对我来说一点儿也___贵。
zh: 这个价格对我来说一点儿也不贵。
py: zhè ge jià gé duì wǒ lái shuō yī diǎn r yě bù guì
en: This price is not expensive at all to me.
why: 'Not at all' needs a negative after 一点儿也. 太 and 很 would turn it into a positive and make the sentence ungrammatical.

q: ___十点了，你怎么还不起床？
zh: 都十点了，你怎么还不起床？
py: dōu shí diǎn le nǐ zěn me hái bù qǐ chuáng
en: It's already ten o'clock. Why aren't you up yet?
why: 都 + time + 了 means 'already', with a complaining tone that fits 怎么还不. 才 would mean 'only ten', the opposite.

q: 你看，我们___等了两个小时了，他怎么还没来？
zh: 你看，我们都等了两个小时了，他怎么还没来？
py: nǐ kàn wǒ men dōu děng le liǎng gè xiǎo shí le tā zěn me hái méi lái
en: Look, we've already waited two hours; why hasn't he come?
why: 都 ... 了 marks 'already so long', matching the complaint. 才 would mean 'only two hours', which does not fit 怎么还没来.

q: 他___三十岁了，还不想买房子。
zh: 他都三十岁了，还不想买房子。
py: tā dōu sān shí suì le hái bù xiǎng mǎi fáng zi
en: He is already thirty and still doesn't want to buy a house.
why: 都 + age + 了 means 'already that old'; 还不想 shows the speaker's surprise. 才 would say 'only thirty' and drop 了.

q: 这个手机___用了五年了，该换新的了。
zh: 这个手机都用了五年了，该换新的了。
py: zhè ge shǒu jī dōu yòng le wǔ nián le gāi huàn xīn de le
en: This phone has already been used for five years; it's time for a new one.
why: 都 ... 了 stresses a long time, which supports 该换新的了. 才 would say 'only five years' and not support replacing it.

q: ___快半夜了，商店早就关门了，你明天再去买吧。
zh: 都快半夜了，商店早就关门了，你明天再去买吧。
py: dōu kuài bàn yè le shāng diàn zǎo jiù guān mén le nǐ míng tiān zài qù mǎi ba
en: It's almost midnight already; the shops closed long ago, so go and buy it tomorrow.
why: 都快...了 means 'already almost'. 才 would say it is still early, which clashes with the shops being closed.

zh: 孩子们都想学游泳。
py: hái zi men dōu xiǎng xué yóu yǒng
en: The children all want to learn to swim.
why: 都 follows the plural subject and comes before the modal 想. It cannot come after 想 or at the end.

zh: 这些鞋都很便宜。
py: zhè xiē xié dōu hěn pián yi
en: All of these shoes are cheap.
why: 都 totals 这些鞋 and goes before 很. 很都便宜 puts it after the degree word and is wrong.

zh: 我们都想买新鞋。
py: wǒ men dōu xiǎng mǎi xīn xié
en: We all want to buy new shoes.
why: 都 follows 我们 and precedes the modal 想. 我们想都买新鞋 is wrong.

zh: 我的同学都喜欢打乒乓球。
py: wǒ de tóng xué dōu xǐ huan dǎ pīng pāng qiú
en: My classmates all like playing table tennis.
why: 都 follows 我的同学 and precedes 喜欢. It cannot follow the verb.

zh: 我们都打算去体育馆打篮球。
py: wǒ men dōu dǎ suàn qù tǐ yù guǎn dǎ lán qiú
en: We all plan to go to the sports hall to play basketball.
why: 都 totals 我们 and goes before 打算 and everything after it. 打算都去 would split the predicate wrongly.

zh: 这些苹果我都买了。
py: zhè xiē píng guǒ wǒ dōu mǎi le
en: I bought all of these apples.
why: 都 can only total something to its left, so 这些苹果 stands before 都. 我都买了这些苹果 leaves 都 nothing to total.

zh: 这两双球鞋我都很喜欢。
py: zhè liǎng shuāng qiú xié wǒ dōu hěn xǐ huan
en: I like both of these pairs of sneakers.
why: The two pairs must stand left of 都 to be totalled. 我都很喜欢这两双球鞋 gives 都 only a single 我.

zh: 比赛的票我们都卖完了。
py: bǐ sài de piào wǒ men dōu mài wán le
en: We have sold all the tickets for the match.
why: The tickets are fronted so 都 can total them: 都 sits before the verb 卖完了.

zh: 那几件打折的衣服妈妈都给姐姐买了。
py: nà jǐ jiàn dǎ zhé de yī fu mā ma dōu gěi jiě jie mǎi le
en: Mum bought all those discounted clothes for my older sister.
why: 都 totals the fronted clothes and stands before the 给 phrase. 给姐姐都买了 would put 都 after the coverb phrase.

zh: 我也喜欢打网球。
py: wǒ yě xǐ huan dǎ wǎng qiú
en: I like playing tennis too.
why: 也 follows the subject and precedes the verb 喜欢. 我喜欢也打网球 puts it after the verb.

zh: 我弟弟也想学游泳。
py: wǒ dì di yě xiǎng xué yóu yǒng
en: My younger brother wants to learn to swim too.
why: 也 comes after the subject, before the modal 想. 我弟弟想也学游泳 puts it in the wrong place.

zh: 这家店的鞋也很贵。
py: zhè jiā diàn de xié yě hěn guì
en: The shoes in this shop are expensive too.
why: 也 goes before 很 and the adjective. It cannot go after 贵 like English 'too'.

zh: 我妹妹也想参加这次游泳比赛。
py: wǒ mèi mei yě xiǎng cān jiā zhè cì yóu yǒng bǐ sài
en: My younger sister wants to take part in this swimming competition too.
why: 也 sits between the subject 我妹妹 and the modal 想, not after 想 or at the end.

zh: 他们也都买了新球拍。
py: tā men yě dōu mǎi le xīn qiú pāi
en: They all bought new rackets too.
why: 也 and 都 are both needed and 也 comes first. 都也 is not possible.

zh: 这些衣服我也都试过了。
py: zhè xiē yī fu wǒ yě dōu shì guo le
en: I have tried on all of these clothes too.
why: The clothes are fronted so 都 can total them, and 也 precedes 都. 都也 is wrong.

zh: 我也不想去。
py: wǒ yě bù xiǎng qù
en: I don't want to go either.
why: 'Not ... either' is 也不. 不也 and 也 at the end of the sentence are both wrong.

zh: 他们都没买球票。
py: tā men dōu méi mǎi qiú piào
en: None of them bought tickets.
why: 都 comes before 没 and means none. 没都买 is not possible.

zh: 我们不都喜欢踢足球。
py: wǒ men bù dōu xǐ huan tī zú qiú
en: Not all of us like playing football.
why: 不 before 都 means 'not all'. 都不喜欢 would say none of us like it.

zh: 我们也都不打算买贵的手机。
py: wǒ men yě dōu bù dǎ suàn mǎi guì de shǒu jī
en: None of us plans to buy expensive phones either.
why: 也 then 都 then 不: 也都不. 'None' needs 都 before 不, and 'either' needs 也 before 都.

zh: 我每天都跑步。
py: wǒ měi tiān dōu pǎo bù
en: I run every day.
why: 每天 is followed by 都 before the verb. 都每天 and 我每天跑步都 are both wrong.

zh: 每个人都要买票。
py: měi gè rén dōu yào mǎi piào
en: Everyone has to buy a ticket.
why: 都 follows 每个人 and precedes 要. It does not go at the end.

zh: 他每次买东西都讨价还价。
py: tā měi cì mǎi dōng xi dōu tǎo jià huán jià
en: He bargains every time he shops.
why: After 每次 ... comes 都 before the verb. 都 cannot come before 每次.

zh: 谁都喜欢这家店。
py: shéi dōu xǐ huan zhè jiā diàn
en: Everyone likes this shop.
why: 谁 is followed by 都 before the verb. 谁喜欢都 puts 都 after the verb.

zh: 我什么都不想买。
py: wǒ shén me dōu bù xiǎng mǎi
en: I don't want to buy anything.
why: The question word 什么 stands before 都 even as the object, then 不 follows. 我不想买什么都 is wrong.

zh: 他什么运动都不喜欢。
py: tā shén me yùn dòng dōu bù xǐ huan
en: He doesn't like any sport.
why: 什么运动 sits before 都 and 不, meaning 'no sport at all'. 他不喜欢什么运动 is the weaker 'doesn't like some sport'.

zh: 他什么时候都可以陪你去买衣服。
py: tā shén me shí hou dōu kě yǐ péi nǐ qù mǎi yī fu
en: He can go clothes shopping with you at any time.
why: 什么时候 + 都 = 'at any time', placed before the modal 可以. 都 cannot follow 可以.

zh: 这件衣服一点儿都不贵。
py: zhè jiàn yī fu yī diǎn r dōu bù guì
en: This garment is not expensive at all.
why: The fixed order is 一点儿, then 都/也, then 不, then the adjective. 不一点儿贵 is wrong.

zh: 他一分钱也没花。
py: tā yī fēn qián yě méi huā
en: He didn't spend a single cent.
why: 'Not a single cent' is 一分钱 + 也 + 没 before the verb. Without 没 the sentence would be affirmative and wrong.

zh: 都十一点了他还没起床。
py: dōu shí yī diǎn le tā hái méi qǐ chuáng
en: It's already eleven and he still isn't up.
why: 都 + time + 了 means 'already'. 了 must stay at the end of the time phrase.

zh: 这双鞋都穿了五年了。
py: zhè shuāng xié dōu chuān le wǔ nián le
en: I've already worn these shoes for five years.
why: 都 comes before the verb phrase with the time amount, and the final 了 closes the 'already' meaning. Without 了 it would sound unfinished.

src_py: wǒ mǎi le zhè xiē yī fu
task: Say you bought ALL of them: put 这些衣服 first and add 都.
zh: 这些衣服我都买了。
py: zhè xiē yī fu wǒ dōu mǎi le
en: I bought all of these clothes.
why: 都 can only total what stands to its left, so the object moves in front of 都. Leaving it after the verb gives 都 nothing to total.

src_py: tā men dōu xǐ huan zhè ge pái zi
task: Say that not all of them like it.
zh: 他们不都喜欢这个牌子。
py: tā men bù dōu xǐ huan zhè ge pái zi
en: Not all of them like this brand.
why: 不 before 都 means 'not all'. 都不喜欢 would mean none of them like it.

src_py: wǒ men dōu qù kàn zú qiú bǐ sài
zh: 我们也都去看足球比赛。
py: wǒ men yě dōu qù kàn zú qiú bǐ sài
en: We are all going to watch the football match too.
why: 也 is added before 都: 也都. The reverse order 都也 is not possible.

src_py: zhè ge qiú pāi hěn zhòng
task: Say it is not heavy at all (use 一点儿).
zh: 这个球拍一点儿都不重。
py: zhè ge qiú pāi yī diǎn r dōu bù zhòng
en: This racket is not heavy at all.
why: 'Not at all' is 一点儿 + 都/也 + 不 + adjective, and 很 is dropped. 不一点儿重 is wrong.

task: Say he does it every weekend (use 每个周末 and 都).
zh: 弟弟每个周末都踢足球。
py: dì di měi gè zhōu mò dōu tī zú qiú
en: My younger brother plays football every weekend.
why: 每个周末 is followed by 都 before the verb. 都 cannot come before 每个周末 or after 踢足球.

s_py: wǒ men qù dōu chāo shì mǎi dōng xi
zh: 我们都去超市买东西。
py: wǒ men dōu qù chāo shì mǎi dōng xi
en: We are all going to the supermarket to buy things.
why: 都 must stand before the verb 去, after the subject it totals. After the verb it is impossible.

s_py: wǒ men dōu zài wǎng shàng mǎi qiú xié
zh: 我们都在网上买球鞋。
py: wǒ men dōu zài wǎng shàng mǎi qiú xié
en: We all buy sneakers online.
why: Correct: 都 comes before the 在 phrase, not after it, and follows the plural subject 我们.

s_py: zhè xiē qiú wǒ mǎi le dōu
zh: 这些球我都买了。
py: zhè xiē qiú wǒ dōu mǎi le
en: I bought all of these balls.
why: 都 cannot end the sentence. It stands right after what it totals (这些球 and 我) and before the verb.

s: 这些票我们都没买到，只好看电视了。
s_py: zhè xiē piào wǒ men dōu méi mǎi dào zhǐ hǎo kàn diàn shì le
zh: 这些票我们都没买到，只好看电视了。
py: zhè xiē piào wǒ men dōu méi mǎi dào zhǐ hǎo kàn diàn shì le
en: We couldn't buy any of these tickets, so we had to watch on TV.
why: Correct: the fronted 这些票 is totalled by 都 and 没 follows 都. 都没 means none of the tickets.

s_py: wǒ xǐ huan hē chá yě
zh: 我也喜欢喝茶。
py: wǒ yě xǐ huan hē chá
en: I like drinking tea too.
why: 也 can never end a sentence the way English 'too' does. It belongs after the subject.

s_py: yě wǒ xiǎng xué dǎ tài jí quán
zh: 我也想学打太极拳。
py: wǒ yě xiǎng xué dǎ tài jí quán
en: I want to learn tai chi too.
why: 也 cannot come before the subject like 'Also,'. It follows the subject and precedes the modal 想.

s_py: nǐ qù yóu yǒng wǒ yě qù
zh: 你去游泳，我也去。
py: nǐ qù yóu yǒng wǒ yě qù
en: You are going swimming; I'll go too.
why: Correct: 也 sits after 我 and before the verb 去. A bare 我也 would not work without a verb.

s_py: xiǎo wáng mǎi yě le yī shuāng qiú xié
zh: 小王也买了一双球鞋。
py: xiǎo wáng yě mǎi le yī shuāng qiú xié
en: Xiao Wang bought a pair of sneakers too.
why: 也 goes before the verb 买, not between the verb and 了.

s_py: tā men dōu yě xǐ huan kàn zú qiú
zh: 他们也都喜欢看足球。
py: tā men yě dōu xǐ huan kàn zú qiú
en: They all like watching football too.
why: The order is always 也都. 都也 does not exist.

s: 这些球鞋我也都试过，但是都不太合适。
s_py: zhè xiē qiú xié wǒ yě dōu shì guo dàn shì dōu bù tài hé shì
zh: 这些球鞋我也都试过，但是都不太合适。
py: zhè xiē qiú xié wǒ yě dōu shì guo dàn shì dōu bù tài hé shì
en: I've tried on all of these sneakers too, but none of them fit very well.
why: Correct: 也都 (in that order) after the fronted object, and 都不 in the second clause means none.

s_py: wǒ bù yě xiǎng qù nà jiā diàn
zh: 我也不想去那家店。
py: wǒ yě bù xiǎng qù nà jiā diàn
en: I don't want to go to that shop either.
why: 也 comes before 不 in 'not ... either'. 不也 is wrong in a plain statement.

s: 他们不都喜欢跑步，有的人更喜欢游泳。
s_py: tā men bù dōu xǐ huan pǎo bù yǒu de rén gèng xǐ huan yóu yǒng
zh: 他们不都喜欢跑步，有的人更喜欢游泳。
py: tā men bù dōu xǐ huan pǎo bù yǒu de rén gèng xǐ huan yóu yǒng
en: Not all of them like running; some prefer swimming.
why: Correct: 不都 means 'not all', which fits the second clause about those who prefer swimming. 都不 would say that none like running.

s: 这些球鞋都不是红色的，有两双是红色的。
s_py: zhè xiē qiú xié dōu bù shì hóng sè de yǒu liǎng shuāng shì hóng sè de
zh: 这些球鞋不都是红色的，有两双是红色的。
py: zhè xiē qiú xié bù dōu shì hóng sè de yǒu liǎng shuāng shì hóng sè de
en: Not all of these sneakers are red; two pairs are red.
why: 都不是 means none are red, which contradicts 'two pairs are red'. 'Not all' needs 不都.

s_py: wǒ men yě dōu méi dài qián
zh: 我们也都没带钱。
py: wǒ men yě dōu méi dài qián
en: None of us brought money either.
why: Correct: 也 then 都, both before 没. 'None ... either' is 也都没.

s_py: tā měi gè zhōu mò tī dōu zú qiú
zh: 他每个周末都踢足球。
py: tā měi gè zhōu mò dōu tī zú qiú
en: He plays football every weekend.
why: 都 goes before the verb, never between the verb and its object.

s: 每个星期六我们都去公园打羽毛球。
s_py: měi gè xīng qī liù wǒ men dōu qù gōng yuán dǎ yǔ máo qiú
zh: 每个星期六我们都去公园打羽毛球。
py: měi gè xīng qī liù wǒ men dōu qù gōng yuán dǎ yǔ máo qiú
en: Every Saturday we go to the park to play badminton.
why: Correct: after the 每 phrase and the subject, 都 comes before the verb 去.

s_py: wǒ shén me bù xiǎng mǎi
zh: 我什么都不想买。
py: wǒ shén me dōu bù xiǎng mǎi
en: I don't want to buy anything.
why: 'Nothing at all' needs 都 (or 也) after 什么 and before 不. Without it the sentence is incomplete.

s: 他什么也没买，只是看了看。
s_py: tā shén me yě méi mǎi zhǐ shì kàn le kan
zh: 他什么也没买，只是看了看。
py: tā shén me yě méi mǎi zhǐ shì kàn le kan
en: He didn't buy anything; he just looked.
why: Correct: in a negative sentence 也 works like 都 after 什么. 什么也没买 means nothing at all.

s_py: zhè ge bāo yī diǎn r yě guì
zh: 这个包一点儿也不贵。
py: zhè ge bāo yī diǎn r yě bù guì
en: This bag isn't expensive at all.
why: 一点儿也 only works with a negative. 不 is required before 贵.

s: 都快十点了，商店怎么还没开门？
s_py: dōu kuài shí diǎn le shāng diàn zěn me hái méi kāi mén
zh: 都快十点了，商店怎么还没开门？
py: dōu kuài shí diǎn le shāng diàn zěn me hái méi kāi mén
en: It's almost ten already; why hasn't the shop opened yet?
why: Correct: 都 ... 了 means 'already', here with 快 and a complaint. It does not mean 'all'.
